subject.title: [Feature]: Support external unified session storage for stateless session mode

question: Should OpenClaw pursue external shared session storage as a core runtime backend, a plugin/SDK storage contract, or defer it behind the broader database-abstraction work?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but backend ownership, config shape, credentials, migrations, consistency semantics, transcript lifecycle, and core-versus-plugin responsibility are product and architecture choices.

options.title: Design Session Storage Contract
options.body: Define a storage-neutral session/transcript contract covering metadata, transcripts, migrations, credentials, consistency, cleanup, and proof before choosing Redis, MongoDB, Postgres, or another backend.

options.title: Defer To Database Abstraction
options.body: Keep this issue as session-specific requirements input while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/94675 decides the broader networked database architecture.

options.title: Document External-Only Stance
options.body: Keep core on local SQLite/files and document sticky sessions or external orchestration as deployment guidance unless a plugin API gap is proven.

recommendation.title: Design Session Storage Contract
recommendation.body: Define a storage-neutral session/transcript contract covering metadata, transcripts, migrations, credentials, consistency, cleanup, and proof before choosing Redis, MongoDB, Postgres, or another backend.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh Lehman is actively coordinating the session/transcript storage migration that this external backend would need to extend or follow.
